title: 1 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Peter chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Peter Chapter 1.

questions.question: In 1 Peter 1, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
Elect according to the foreknowledge of God the Father
Who are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation ready to be revealed in the last time
questions.correctAnswer: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
questions.explanation: This greeting by Peter appears first in 1 Peter 1:1

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:2, through what means are the elect sanctified?
options: Through faith in their own strength
questions.explanation: The verse states the elect are sanctified through sanctification of the Spirit

questions.question: What has God the Father begotten us again to, according to 1 Peter 1:3?
options: A lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead
questions.correctAnswer: A lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:3 says God has begotten us again unto a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ

questions.question: What kind of inheritance is reserved in heaven for believers, according to 1 Peter 1:4?
options: Incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away
questions.correctAnswer: Incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away
questions.explanation: The inheritance described in 1 Peter 1:4 is incorruptible, undefiled, and fadeth not away

questions.question: By what power are believers kept unto salvation, according to 1 Peter 1:5?
options: By the power of God through faith
questions.correctAnswer: By the power of God through faith
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:5 states believers are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation

questions.question: What causes believers to be in heaviness for a season, according to 1 Peter 1:6?
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says believers are in heaviness through manifold temptations

questions.question: What is the trial of faith compared to in 1 Peter 1:7?
options: More precious than gold that perisheth
questions.correctAnswer: More precious than gold that perisheth
questions.explanation: The trial of faith is described as much more precious than gold that perisheth in 1 Peter 1:7

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:8, what kind of joy do believers have when they believe in Jesus whom they have not seen?
options: Joy unspeakable and full of glory
questions.correctAnswer: Joy unspeakable and full of glory
questions.explanation: Believers rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory according to 1 Peter 1:8

questions.question: What are believers receiving as the end of their faith, according to 1 Peter 1:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:9 states believers receive the salvation of their souls as the end of their faith

questions.question: To whom is Peter writing in 1 Peter 1:1?
options: Strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
questions.correctAnswer: Strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia
questions.explanation: Peter addresses the strangers scattered throughout those regions in 1 Peter 1:1

questions.question: What blessing does Peter wish the elect in 1 Peter 1:2?
questions.explanation: Peter wishes that grace and peace be multiplied to the elect in 1 Peter 1:2

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Peter 1:3, God has begotten believers again according to His abundant mercy.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:3 states God, according to His abundant mercy, hath begotten us again

questions.question: True or False: 1 Peter 1:4 describes the inheritance reserved in heaven as fading away.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:4 states the inheritance is incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away

questions.question: True or False: 1 Peter 1:7 says the trial of faith is tested by fire.
questions.explanation: The verse says the trial of faith is tried with fire

questions.question: True or False: 1 Peter 1:5 states believers are kept by the power of angels unto salvation.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:5 states believers are kept by the power of God through faith, not by angels

medium.title: 1 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Peter Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who enquired and searched diligently about the salvation mentioned in 1 Peter 1:10?
questions.explanation: This is correct as 1 Peter 1:10 states that 'the prophets have enquired and searched diligently' about the salvation.

questions.question: What will happen if you hope to the end for the grace to be brought at the revelation of Jesus Christ according to 1 Peter 1:13?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:13 encourages believers to hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought at the revelation of Jesus Christ, indicating they will receive grace.

questions.question: What does 1 Peter 1:11 indicate that the Spirit of Christ testified about?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:11 mentions that the Spirit of Christ testified beforehand 'the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that should follow'.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter 1:12 describe the things that were ministered to those now receiving the gospel?
options: For the sake of the prophets
questions.explanation: According to 1 Peter 1:12, these things were ministered 'which are now reported unto you' and 'the angels desire to look into'.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:14, how should believers not fashion themselves?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:14 instructs believers to be 'not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance'.

questions.question: What is the call to holiness based on in 1 Peter 1:16?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:16 states, 'Be ye holy; for I am holy,' indicating holiness is based on the nature of God.

questions.question: What does 1 Peter 1:17 say about God’s judgment?
options: He judges without respect of persons
questions.correctAnswer: He judges without respect of persons
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:17 states that God 'without respect of persons judgeth according to every man's work'.

questions.question: What should believers do during their time of sojourning according to 1 Peter 1:17?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:17 instructs believers to 'pass the time of your sojourning here in fear'.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:18, what were believers not redeemed with?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:18 states that believers were 'not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold'.

questions.question: What is the relationship between trials and faith according to 1 Peter 1:7?
options: Trials are a sign of failure
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:7 indicates that 'the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth', shows that faith is refined through trials.

questions.question: What is the ultimate outcome of faith according to 1 Peter 1:9?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:9 states that believers are 'Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls'.

questions.question: What does 1 Peter 1:8 say about believing in Christ without seeing Him?
options: It is a sign of weakness
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:8 states that 'Whom having not seen, ye love;... ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory', indicating that faith brings joy.

questions.question: True or False: The prophets prophesied for their own benefit according to 1 Peter 1:12.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:12 states that the prophets ministered the things 'not unto themselves, but unto us', indicating their prophecies were for others.

questions.question: True or False: Believers are encouraged to fashion themselves according to their past ignorance in 1 Peter 1:14.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:14 advises believers to be 'not fashioning yourselves according to the former lusts in your ignorance', which means they should not do so.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Peter 1:16 commands believers to be holy because God is holy.
questions.explanation: This is correct as 1 Peter 1:16 explicitly states, 'Be ye holy; for I am holy'.

hard.title: 1 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Peter Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:19, by what means were believers redeemed?
options: With the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot
By the works of the law
questions.correctAnswer: With the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:19 clearly states believers were redeemed 'with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot,' emphasizing the sacrificial nature of Christ's atonement.

questions.question: What does 1 Peter 1:20 say about Christ's foreordination?
options: He was foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for you
He was created at the beginning of time
He was born at the appointed time without prior planning
questions.correctAnswer: He was foreordained before the foundation of the world but manifest in these last times for you
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:20 explains that Christ was 'foreordained before the foundation of the world' but was revealed in the last times for believers, showing God's eternal plan.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:21, what purpose does God’s raising of Christ from the dead serve?
options: That your faith and hope might be in God
That Jesus might reign as king of Israel
That the law might be fulfilled
That the temple might be rebuilt
questions.correctAnswer: That your faith and hope might be in God
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:21 specifically states God raised Christ and gave Him glory 'that your faith and hope might be in God,' linking resurrection to believer's trust.

questions.question: In 1 Peter 1:22, what is the result of obeying the truth through the Spirit?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:22 teaches that obeying the truth through the Spirit purifies souls and results in 'unfeigned love of the brethren,' emphasizing genuine Christian love.

questions.question: What does 1 Peter 1:23 say about the nature of the new birth?
options: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God
Being born of flesh and blood
Being born through rituals and ceremonies
Being born according to human traditions
questions.correctAnswer: Being born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:23 emphasizes the spiritual new birth is 'not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible, by the word of God,' highlighting the eternal nature of God's word and new life.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:25, what is said about the word of the Lord?
options: The word of the Lord endureth for ever
The word of the Lord is temporary
The word of the Lord changes with time
The word of the Lord is only for the Jews
questions.correctAnswer: The word of the Lord endureth for ever
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:25 teaches that 'the word of the Lord endureth for ever,' contrasting the fleeting nature of human life with the eternal stability of God's word.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'anepilēmptos' in 1 Peter 1:19 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'anepilēmptos' in 1 Peter 1:19 means 'without blemish,' describing Christ as the perfect sacrificial Lamb without defect.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in 1 Peter 1:24-25 comparing human life and God's word?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:24-25 uses contrast and parallelism by comparing 'all flesh is as grass' which withers, with 'the word of the Lord endureth for ever,' highlighting temporal vs eternal.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of holiness in 1 Peter 1:16?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:16 quotes 'Be ye holy; for I am holy,' which is a direct reference to Leviticus 11:44, linking New Testament holiness to Old Testament commands.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of salvation by precious blood found in 1 Peter 1:18-19?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 9:14 speaks of Christ's blood as the eternal Spirit offering, echoing 1 Peter 1:18-19's theme of redemption by the precious blood of Christ.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the statement about redemption with the precious blood of Christ in 1 Peter 1:19?
options: That ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold
Be ye holy; for I am holy
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ
Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind
questions.correctAnswer: That ye were not redeemed with corruptible things, as silver and gold
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:18 immediately precedes 1 Peter 1:19 by stating believers were not redeemed with corruptible things like silver and gold, setting context for redemption by Christ's blood.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter 1:7 use the metaphor of gold to describe faith?
options: Faith is more precious than gold that perisheth, though it is tried with fire
Faith is like gold that can be bought
Faith is worthless like fool's gold
Faith is hidden like gold in the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is more precious than gold that perisheth, though it is tried with fire
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:7 uses the metaphor that the trial of faith is more precious than perishable gold, refined by fire, emphasizing the purifying nature of trials.

questions.question: What typology is present in 1 Peter 1:19 calling Christ 'a lamb without blemish and without spot'?
options: Christ as the fulfillment of the Old Testament Passover lamb
Christ as a priest of Aaron’s line
questions.correctAnswer: Christ as the fulfillment of the Old Testament Passover lamb
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:19’s description of Christ as 'a lamb without blemish' typologically connects to the Passover lamb in Exodus, symbolizing sacrifice for deliverance.

questions.question: According to 1 Peter 1:13, what three exhortations are given to believers for their mindset?
options: Gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end
Relax and trust only, be joyful always, and ignore trials
Seek wealth, avoid suffering, and be popular
questions.correctAnswer: Gird up the loins of your mind, be sober, and hope to the end
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:13 exhorts believers to mentally prepare ('gird up the loins of your mind'), be sober-minded, and maintain hope to the end, encouraging spiritual discipline.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Peter 1:23, the new birth is described as being born of corruptible seed.
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:23 states believers are 'born again, not of corruptible seed, but of incorruptible,' so the new birth is specifically not of corruptible seed.

theological.title: 1 Peter Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Peter Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Peter 1:2 teach about salvation?
options: Salvation is by election according to the foreknowledge of God the Father through sanctification of the Spirit and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ
Salvation is earned by human effort and obedience to the law
Salvation is only for the Jewish people as God's chosen nation
Salvation depends on performing religious rituals perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation is by election according to the foreknowledge of God the Father through sanctification of the Spirit and the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:2 teaches that believers are elect according to God's foreknowledge, sanctified by the Spirit, and cleansed by the blood of Christ, emphasizing divine initiative in salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Peter 1:23 teach about the new birth?
options: The new birth is a spiritual regeneration by the incorruptible word of God
The new birth is a physical rebirth through natural descent
The new birth is achieved by human wisdom and knowledge
The new birth is an outward ritual without inward change
questions.correctAnswer: The new birth is a spiritual regeneration by the incorruptible word of God
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:23 states believers are born again not of corruptible but incorruptible seed through the living and abiding word of God, teaching spiritual regeneration by divine means.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Peter 1:19 teach about the nature of Christ's atonement?
options: Christ's atonement is by the precious blood of a lamb without blemish and without spot
Christ's atonement is by human sacrifices and rituals
Christ's atonement is symbolic and not actual
Christ's atonement is through moral example only
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's atonement is by the precious blood of a lamb without blemish and without spot
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:19 emphasizes the precious and sinless nature of Christ’s sacrificial death, portraying Him as the spotless lamb whose blood redeems believers.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 1 Peter 1:3 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:3 blesses God for His abundant mercy in giving new birth to believers through Christ’s resurrection, highlighting God's merciful nature.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 1 Peter 1:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:17 describes God as the impartial judge who judges according to every man’s work, demonstrating divine justice.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter 1:13 connect to the broader biblical theme of eschatological hope?
options: It calls believers to hope for the grace to be revealed at Jesus Christ’s coming, linking present sanctification with future glorification
It teaches that believers should renounce all hope in this life
It connects hope solely with earthly prosperity and success
It rejects any future revelation of grace or glory
questions.correctAnswer: It calls believers to hope for the grace to be revealed at Jesus Christ’s coming, linking present sanctification with future glorification
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:13 exhorts believers to hope fully for the grace at Christ’s revelation, tying present Christian conduct to future eschatological fulfillment.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter 1:10-12 relate to the Old Testament prophetic anticipation of Christ’s suffering and glory?
options: It shows that the prophets diligently searched and prophesied about the grace and sufferings of Christ, which now apply to the New Testament believers
It claims the prophets were ignorant and did not understand their own prophecies
It denies any connection between the Old Testament and New Testament revelation
It says the prophets only spoke about earthly kingdoms
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that the prophets diligently searched and prophesied about the grace and sufferings of Christ, which now apply to the New Testament believers
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:10-12 explains that Old Testament prophets searched for the meaning of their prophecies concerning Christ’s sufferings and glory, which are now revealed to New Testament believers.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Peter 1:18 and 1 Peter 1:19 teach about redemption?
options: Redemption is not by perishable things like silver or gold but by the precious blood of Christ, a spotless lamb
Redemption is by human tradition and rituals
Redemption can be earned by good works and moral behavior
Redemption is unnecessary because sin is not real
questions.correctAnswer: Redemption is not by perishable things like silver or gold but by the precious blood of Christ, a spotless lamb
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:18-19 teaches that believers were redeemed not with corruptible things but by the precious and spotless blood of Christ, highlighting the superiority of Christ’s atonement.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Peter 1:21 and 1 Peter 1:22 teach about faith and love?
options: Faith in God who raised Christ leads to purified souls and fervent, sincere love among believers
Faith is irrelevant to Christian life and love is optional
Faith leads to isolation and rejection of community
Love is based on human effort without spiritual influence
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in God who raised Christ leads to purified souls and fervent, sincere love among believers
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:21-22 links faith in God’s resurrection power to the purification of souls and sincere, fervent brotherly love, indicating the transformative work of faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Peter 1:4 and 1 Peter 1:5 teach about the believer’s inheritance and security?
options: Believers have an incorruptible inheritance reserved in heaven and are kept by God's power through faith unto salvation
Believers inherit earthly wealth and possessions guaranteed by works
Believers’ inheritance is uncertain and can be lost at any time
Believers are saved by themselves without divine protection
questions.correctAnswer: Believers have an incorruptible inheritance reserved in heaven and are kept by God's power through faith unto salvation
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:4-5 teaches that believers possess an imperishable heavenly inheritance and are guarded by God's power through faith until salvation is fully revealed.

questions.question: Skeptics claim 1 Peter 1:6-7 teaches that suffering indicates God’s rejection of believers. What does 1 Peter 1:6-7 actually teach?
options: Suffering is a temporary trial that tests faith and results in praise, honor, and glory at Christ’s appearing
Suffering proves that believers are abandoned by God
Suffering is meaningless and without purpose
Suffering should be avoided at all costs to maintain faith
questions.correctAnswer: Suffering is a temporary trial that tests faith and results in praise, honor, and glory at Christ’s appearing
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:6-7 clarifies that present manifold temptations refine faith like gold tested by fire, producing praise and glory at Jesus’ return, not divine rejection.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Peter 1:16 teach about Christian holiness?
options: Believers are called to be holy because God Himself is holy
Holiness is optional and not essential for believers
Holiness is only an external appearance
Holiness means separation from society by physical isolation
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to be holy because God Himself is holy
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:16 commands holiness as a reflection of God’s own holiness, rooting Christian ethical conduct in God’s character.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 1 Peter 1:20 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:20 shows Christ was foreordained before the foundation of the world, demonstrating God’s sovereign, eternal plan of redemption.

questions.question: How does 1 Peter 1:25 relate to the overall biblical theme of the enduring word of God?
options: It declares the word of the Lord endures forever, contrasting human mortality with divine permanence
It claims the word of God is temporary and subject to change
It suggests human words are superior to God’s word
It teaches that the word of God is irrelevant to salvation
questions.correctAnswer: It declares the word of the Lord endures forever, contrasting human mortality with divine permanence
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:25 contrasts the fleeting nature of human life with the eternal endurance of God’s word, underscoring its unchanging authority.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 Peter 1:14 and 1 Peter 1:15 teach about Christian obedience and holiness?
options: Believers are called to obedient, holy living, not conforming to former lusts but reflecting God’s holiness
Obedience and holiness are unnecessary for Christians
Holiness means adopting worldly values to fit in
Obedience is based on fear of punishment alone
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to obedient, holy living, not conforming to former lusts but reflecting God’s holiness
questions.explanation: 1 Peter 1:14-15 teaches believers to live obediently and be holy as God is holy, rejecting former sinful desires, emphasizing ethical transformation.
